body:
Against the binary in the jail (zmx 0.8.1, scratch ZMX_DIR), because brief-v0 said the source wins over the notes.

1. `--labels` takes exactly one argv element. `zmx attach --labels project=P id=ID n1` creates a session literally named `id=ID`; the form that works is one element, `--labels "project=P id=ID"`. A repeated `--labels` is not additive — the last one wins — so a wrapper mixing its labels with a caller's must build one token.
2. `attach --labels` upserts onto an *existing* session (a session holding only `state=working` gained `b=2` while an attach ran). So 'an existing session is never relabelled' is a check the wrapper must make, not a property of zmx.
3. `zmx run NAME true` creates the session and prints `session "NAME" created` plus a ZMX_TASK_COMPLETED marker on stdout. `run` takes no labels, so the creation path is a dispatch of its own and its output is not the caller's.
4. `zmx get missing` exits 1 with 'error: session ... not found or unresponsive'. `zmx ls --short` lists names only, one per line, exits 0 when empty — the cheaper existence test, and the one that does not touch the session.
5. `zmx run . CMD` fails outside a session: `.` is a print-env/history convention, not a run one. Exit codes propagate exactly (`false` gives 1, `sh -c 'exit 7'` gives 7), and a detached run returns 0 at once with 'command sent!'.
title: Five probes that shaped the wrapper
